steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place sliced apples in a large bowl; sprinkle with lemon juice. Mix white sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, cinnamon, and nutmeg together in a small bowl; sprinkle mixture over apples and toss until evenly coated. Stir in raisins and walnuts; transfer mixture into pie shell.
Mix 1/2 cup flour and brown sugar together in a small bowl. Blend in butter with a fork until mixture is crumbly; sprinkle over apple filling. Cover top of pie loosely with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake until top is golden brown and filling is bubbly, about 25 to 30 minutes more. Cool on a wire rack before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Crumb Pie
raw_recipe.description: This crumb topping for apple pie will add a delicious crunch. You can add walnuts and raisins to this juicy apple pie to make it even dreamier!

review.reviewBody: I made this for Thanksgiving and it was incredible! The entire family loved it and it was actually the only pie that was completely gone at the end of the day! The only thing I changed was to double the amount of crumb topping, I just didn't think it was enough, it didn't cover the entire top of the pie. We warmed each slice in the microwave for 35 seconds and topped with Cool Whip--excellent!! My other apple pie recipes will be deleted from my recipe box!!! Thanks for a wonderful recipe!!

This recipe is amazing!!!! I made 2 pies and both were finished within 24 hours. Only one person said it was too sweet. It is very sweet, but it's as sweet as apple pie should be. However, I will use less sugar next time because I'm sure it will still be great even if I used a little less in the filling. Changes I made included doubling the flour in the filling to prevent it being too watery as other reviewers mentioned, and I added an extra tablespoon of butter to the crumble as well as adding 50% more of all ingredients to have enough of the topping. I also cooked it covered for 40 min and uncovered for 30 min, then allowed it to cook for 1-2 hours before cutting. It was perfect! Next time I will place aluminum foil under the dish to catch any spillage for easy clean up (some filling did spill out while cooking uncovered).

Followed the recipe, except I had Apple Pie Spice in my spice cupard, so used that in place of the other spices and it was delicious. Also covered the pie with Aluminum Foil for First 15 minutes, then removed foil and continued baking the remainder of the time suggested. It came out a beautiful golden brown. My guest said it was the best Apple Crumb Pie they had ever had. I also served with a scoop of Vanilla Ice Cream. YUM!

Use fold-out crust. Free form it! 

Use 7-8 GREEN apples. Peel and cut into approximately 1/2 pieces. 
Be sure you mix all filling ingredients in bowl before stirring in cut apples. 
Use 1 cup sugar for filling. Too tart otherwise.
I used a bit more cinnamon. 
Double topping mixture. You’ll need it to cover.

Breyer’s vanilla ice cream on top! Otherwise, what’s the point?

This is our go to apple pie recipe. Delicious but too sweet for our taste. Reduce sugar in both apple and crumb topping and it should do the trick. I followed recipe with one small addition... 1/4t. Corn starch to the flour sugar cinnamon nutmeg mixture the apples are tossed in. Was afraid of too much liquid based on previous reviews. It made for a lovely caramel-like coating around well cooked apples. Used mandolin for uniformly sliced apples, thin worked great as we like a well cooked apple in our pies. Will make again, just less sugar.

I love this apple crumb pie. I’ve been making my own pie crusts and wanted to branch out from quiche - this was a great option in light of my crust being questionable for topping for a traditional apple pie. I blind baked my crust for about 10 minutes at 350° while I was prepping the filling. I also added a dash of clove to the filling and it really enhanced that lovely fall flavor. This is a great dish, and aside from the clove I didn’t change it. Enjoy!

I have made this twice now. I chose Honeycrisp apples and did choose to use lemon juice after sampling the apples I got. I was leary of raisins and walnuts but wanted to see so I just scattered some of each. Well, we absolutely loved it. S much so, we have declared it to be the best apple pie that we have ever tasted! My husband says it is apple pie crack; it is that good to him!
Ingredient choices are everything so I would like to note that 1) I used a raisin medley that I got from bulk food section of Winco, and 2) I always toast my nuts for baking after learning about the improved flavor from America's Test Kitchen.
*Using Honey Crisp apples gave me a pie that was not runny. I don't know if that is what can make a difference or not for those who used Granny Smith apples.

Rock-solid recipe. Followed it closely, but also added crushed pecans and in the second one, a small box of raisins, too. Tossed in a shake of ground clove to the apple coating. I used Gala apples that were just a bit too soft for eating, IMO. Keebler shortbread crust.

Made this for Easter and was amazing. I did add the lemon juice and increased flour in apples to 3TBS. I doubled the crumb topping but think I will decrease the sugar in the topping next time. Also used margarine instead of butter since we are vegan.
I made this pie for my granddaughter and it tasted great except a little too much liquid in the pie. I think next time I will add 4 tablespoons of flour instead of 2. I used Granny Smith apples.

I did make some changes. I used granny smith apples. I used 1c fresh cranberries instead of raisins/walnuts. I changed the crumble - I added 1c quick oats and doubled the butter. Used raw sugar instead of brown sugar. It was not runny at all as some others had noted using the recipe as written. It was not too sweet as the cranberries and green apples balanced it well. It came out perfect and was festive looking for Thanksgiving. Planning to make again at Christmas we enjoyed it so much!

I followed the recipe to the T, except for the lemon juice… Unfortunately the pie was too sugary, and too much soupy liquid at the bottom of the pie dish when finished. The crumble did not “crumble”…it was too powdery. Sadly, I will not try this recipe again.

I made 3 pies, one for myself and 2 for neighbors who have helped me. One gentleman took 2 bites and teared up, had to stop to dab his eyes, saying "that's the kindest thing and most delicious pie I can ever remember in my life." I did not see that coming. The pie was scrumptious, but the encounter was a true blessing.
I love making this apple pie. I use a different crumble because I never got this one to come out but non the less it's super good.

The crumble was finicky to get to the right texture but it was so worth it. I thought this was the best thing I've tasted! Best eaten cooled the day of baking while the crumble is still crunchy. The apples I used were too tart (Bramley) so next time I'll try another type. Also, I ended up using only around 1.5 lbs of apple.

crumble was runny, my pie was swimming in butter. When I saw the consistency of it before putting it on top, I knew it was too much butter, not crumbly/dry enough, but I decided to not question the recipe and go ahead. BIG MISTAKE! Thanks for ruining thanksgiving lol
I had the same experience as another rater, in that the topping was runny and not crumbly. It had a good flavor but the texture was not “crumbly”.
I made my own pie filling and followed the recipe for crust. Absolutely love it, so crunchy and an awesome shortcut traditional pie crust. I added chooped pecans as well.
